name: cat-decision-dynamics
title: Decision Dynamics (Catch vs Avoid)
question:
How do the CTRNN's internal dynamics differ when the agent commits to catching
a circle versus avoiding a diamond presented at the same offset?
hypothesis:
The neuron-output trajectories (and the motor-neuron phase trajectory) start
together and then separate by category, showing that the decision is a
divergence in the coupled system's state over time, not a discrete switch.
objective:
Record the neuron outputs over a circle trial and a diamond trial at offset +3
and compare them, including the two motor neurons' phase trajectory.
claim:
The coupled neural dynamics commit differently to the two categories: outputs
and the motor-neuron phase trajectory diverge after a shared initial phase.
description:
The committed seed is run at offset +3 for a circle and a diamond; per-step
neuron outputs are recorded and plotted. This connects the behaviour to Beer's
dynamical reading of the decision.

expected_behavior.name: neural-trajectories-separate-by-category
expected_behavior.condition: committed seed, offset +3, circle vs diamond, 200 steps @ dt=0.1
expected_behavior.rationale:
The two trials share an early trajectory (active perception) then separate,
and the motor-neuron phase trajectory traces distinct paths for catch vs
avoid — the signature of a decision made in the system's state dynamics.

findings.summary: Neural trajectories share an early phase then diverge by category; motor-neuron phase paths differ.
findings.detail:
figures/decision_dynamics.png (left) shows neuron outputs for circle vs
diamond overlapping early then separating; (right) the two motor neurons'
phase trajectory traces distinct loops for catch vs avoid.
